title: Protocol for influenza A virus infection of mice and viral load determination
protocol: Prepare a heating pad with small inclination to place mice while under anesthesia.
Weigh the mice.
Anaesthetize mice by intraperitoneal injection of 0.05 mL/10 g bodyweight of anesthesia mix.
Pipette 40 μL of the IAV dilution slowly and steadily into one nostril of the anaesthetized mouse.
Pinch the footpad to make the mouse take a deep breath after inoculation.
Place the mouse on the heating pad until it wakes up.
Periodically check breathing and reflexes of the mouse.
Place the mouse back in the cage only after it is able to flip from supine position and move its hind legs.
Apply an ophthalmic ointment to the eyes if anesthesia lasts longer than 5 minutes.
Terminally anesthetize mice by i.p. injection of 0.1 mL/10 g of anesthesia mix 2.
Collect blood by retro-orbital bleeding to a 1.5 mL tube.
Allow the blood to clot by leaving it undisturbed at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge at approximately 8,500×g for 10 minutes in a table centrifuge at 20°C.
Collect serum into clean 0.5 mL tubes in aliquots.
Store sera at -80°C to avoid freeze-thaw cycles.
Dissect the mouse and place it on its back on a surgical plate.
Fix the limbs by pinning them down.
Spray the skin with 70% ethanol for disinfection.
Remove the skin to expose the trachea.
Cut the salivary glands and sternohyoid muscle to expose the trachea.
Make a small incision in the trachea with scissors carefully.
Load 500 μL of PBS into a 1 mL syringe with detachable needle.
Assemble a catheter with the syringe.
Insert the catheter into the trachea and gently inject the PBS.
Gently aspirate the solution back to the syringe.
Transfer the recovered BAL fluid into a 1.5 mL tube on ice.
Repeat the procedure once again.
Be careful that the catheter is not inserted too far into the trachea.
If no fluid is aspirated back in the syringe, carefully move the catheter up and down into the trachea.
Separate the cellular and noncellular components of the BAL fluid.
Centrifuge at ∼ 230×g for 10 min in a table centrifuge at 4°C.
Collect the BAL supernatant (S/N) into clean 0.5 mL tubes in aliquots.
The BAL S/N should be used immediately fresh for viral determination by plaque assay.
Pause point: The BAL S/N can be stored at −80°C for several months before performing viral HA ELISA.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 0.5 ml of PBS + 1% FBS.

Use the resuspended cells for downstream applications, including inflammatory cell influx analysis in the lung, FACS analysis, and determination of infectious viral load in sorted cells by plaque assay.
Dissect the right lobe for RNA or viral load assessment by plaque assay.
Make an incision in the thorax to make the lung visible.
Knot tightly around the right main airway.
Remove the right lobe of the lung, leaving the right airway sealed.
Transfer immediately the right lobe into a 2 ml tube and snap-freeze in liquid N2.
Pause point: The frozen lung tissues can be stored at −80°C for several months before performing RNA isolation.
Dissect the left lobe for histology.
Make a loose surgical node around the trachea with a piece of suture.
Load 350 μL of 4% PFA/OCT embedding medium mix in a 2:1 ratio into a 1 mL syringe with detachable needle.
Assemble a catheter with the syringe.
Insert the catheter into the trachea and left main airway, then gently inject the mix to inflate.
Remove the catheter while tightening the surgical node around the trachea until completely removed.
Dissect the left lung together with the trachea and place in a 7 mL polystyrene bijou bottle filled with 5 mL of 4% PFA.
Leave overnight at 4°C, ensuring the lung is submerged by hooking the suture as you close the lid.
Rinse tissues briefly in PBS and place in a fresh 7 mL polystyrene bijou bottle filled with 5 mL of 30% sucrose in PBS.
Leave overnight at 4°C for cryopreservation.
Embed tissues in OCT medium to perform cryosectioning.
Perfuse the lung with 10 mL PBS via the right heart ventricle.
Remove the lung and cut it into small pieces with a scalpel.
Transfer the lung pieces in 3 mL digest solution.
Place the mixture in a rotator set at 37°C for 1 hour.
Perform occasional trituration with a 1 mL pipette during incubation.
Pass the mixture through a 100 μm cell strainer at the end of the incubation.
Wash the cells with FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the cells at 200×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer.
Keep the single-cell suspension on ice until staining.
If residual red blood cells remain, add 1 mL of red blood cell lysing buffer to the cell pellet and incubate on ice for 15 minutes.
Wash the cells with 20 mL of FACS buffer after lysis.
Centrifuge the cells at 200×g for 10 minutes at 4°C after washing.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer after centrifugation.
Homogenize frozen lungs collected in step 11 using TriReagent.
Immediately homogenize the mixture with a mechanical homogenizer at maximum speed (30,000 rpm) for approximately 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the homogenized lung samples at 10,000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Autoclave the homogenizer before use.
Wash the homogenizer with DEPC-treated dH2O between samples if more than one sample is analyzed.
Add 200 μL of chloroform to the sample and shake vigorously by hand for 15 seconds.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 2–3 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at approximately 10,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the upper transparent phase and transfer it into a fresh 1.5 mL tube.
Add 500 μL of isopropanol to precipitate the RNA and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at approximately 10,000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and wash the pellet with 1 mL 75% EtOH.
Mix by hand and centrifuge the mixture at approximately 3,300×g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant completely.
Air-dry RNA pellets.
Dissolve RNA in 50 μL of RNase DNase-free ddH2O and incubate at 57°C in a heat block for 10 minutes.
Store RNA samples at -80°C until use.
Measure O.D. (1:50) on a spectrophotometer at 260 nm to calculate concentration.
Run 1 μg of RNA in a 1.5% agarose gel to monitor RNA integrity.
Treat 2 μg of RNA with RQ1 DNase and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Stop the reaction with 1 μL RQ1 Stop Solution at 65°C for 10 minutes.
Add 1 μL of random primers to the sample and incubate at 70°C for 5 minutes.
Perform reverse transcription with M-MLV reverse transcriptase in the presence of RNaseOUT at 37°C for 60 minutes.
Determine viral load by real-time qPCR analysis.
Prepare qPCR master mix using primers for IAV PR8 NS1 gene.
Run reaction at 59°C for 40 cycles.
Calculate relative amounts of NS1 RNA expression normalized to Gapdh or Ppia according to the ΔΔCT method.
Coat a plate with capture antibody.
Dilute capture antibody (stock concentration: 1 mg/mL) to working concentration (2 μg/mL) in PBS.
Coat a 96-well microplate with 100 μL per well of the diluted capture antibody.
Seal the plate and incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash the plate.
Wash the plate with 300 μL wash buffer per well.
Three washes of the plate are recommended.
Remove any remaining wash buffer by inverting the plate and blotting it against clean and dry paper towels.
Block unspecific binding.
Add 300 μL of blocking buffer to each well.
Incubate at RT on a plate shaker for 1 hour.
Perform serial dilutions to achieve consistency for the final dilution of 1:100 by performing two dilutions of 1:10 each.
Prepare the HA standard by performing serial 2-fold dilutions in 7 tubes, one for each dilution of the standard curve.
Add 500 μL of sample dilution buffer to six of the tubes.
Calculate and add the volume of the stock standard needed to have a starting concentration of 3000 pg/mL in 1000 μL of sample dilution buffer, mix well.

Transfer 500 μL of the prepared working standard to the second tube to have a concentration of 1500 pg/mL, mix well by pipetting and continue until the lowest recommended concentration (46,875 pg/mL) is achieved.
Repeat wash step #20 after blocking.
Pipette 100 μL per well of samples or standards.
Seal the plate and incubate for 2 h at RT on a plate shaker.

Prepare the detection antibody by diluting it (stock concentration: 0.2 mg/mL) to working concentration (0.5 μg/mL) in HA ELISA detection antibody dilution buffer, 10 min before the end of the incubation period.
Repeat wash step #20 after incubation.
Pipette 100 μL of the detection antibody to each well.
Seal the plate and incubate for 1 h at RT on a plate shaker.
Repeat wash step #20.
Pipette 200 μL of substrate solution to each well.
Incubate for ∼20 min at RT, by monitoring the development of blue color.
Avoid placing the plate in direct light during incubation.
Pipette 50 μL of stop solution to each well.
Gently tap the plate to ensure thorough mixing.
Measure the OD immediately in a microplate reader set to 450 nm.
Calculate the mean absorbance for each set of duplicate standards and samples.
Subtract the mean zero standard absorbance from each sample's absorbance.
Use the mean absorbance for each one of the seven standards at the y-axis and their concentration at the x-axis to construct a curve through the seven points of the graph.
Use the absorbance of the unknown samples to calculate the corresponding concentration through the standard curve.
If samples are diluted, multiply the calculated concentration by the dilution factor.
Aspirate the medium from 12-well plates with MDCK cells.
Wash the monolayers twice with PBS.
Leave the cells in PBS until required.
Add 405 μL of MDCK infection medium to each tube.
Add 45 μL of sample to the first tube and vortex well.
Perform 10-fold serial dilutions throughout all tubes.
Remove the PBS from the cells.
Add 200 μL of inoculum in each well.
Infect cells for 1 h at 37°C.
Gently rock the plates every 20 min during infection.
Prepare overlay medium for each 12-well plate using 9.1 mL of medium.
Aliquot overlay medium in 15 mL tubes and pre-warm them in a 37°C incubator.
Melt 2% agar solution in dH2O by microwaving for about 2 min.
Cool the melted agar to 65°C in a water bath until ready to use.
Remove inoculums from the 12-well plates after infection.
Mix 3.9 mL of agar solution with pre-warmed overlay medium and add 2 μg/mL TPCK-treated trypsin.
Gently add 1 mL of the agar overlay medium to each well.
Allow agar overlay to dry for 10 min in the laminar flow hood.
Place plates upside-down in the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Visualize plaques starting from day 2 post plating.
Count plaques with a naked eye by viewing the plate under a light source.
Carefully remove agar from the plates using a small spatula.
Fix and stain cells by adding 1 mL of crystal violet stain/well for at least 10 min.
Gently wash off the stain with running water.
Leave the plates to air-dry at room temperature.
Recount the number of plaques after drying.
Determine viral titers by counting plaques in each well and calculating averages.
Determine the viral titer of the initial viral suspension according to the given formula.
Count plaques in replicates of the 10−2 dilution of Sample 1.
Calculate the average number of plaques for Sample 1.
Use the formula: (average number of plaques/10−dilution) * (1 mL/volume of sample used for infection).
Influenza A dilutions at 10−3 and 10−4 are used as positive controls for plaque formation.
Serum-free medium is used as a negative control.
Assess infectious viral load by performing a plaque assay in cells.
Time required for the plaque assay: 3 days.
Count viable cells from the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) or lung single cell suspension using trypan blue.
Exclude dead cells stained with trypan blue.
Adjust the cell concentration to 1 × 10^7 cells/mL in FACS buffer.
Incubate cells with anti-mouse CD16/32 antibody diluted at a ratio of 1:100 for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Stain cells with specific antibodies.
Add appropriate cell-specific antibodies against EpCAM and CD45 at a 1:100 dilution directly to the cell suspension.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash with 10 times the volume of FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Filter through a polystyrene test tube with a cell strainer cap.
Add DAPI at a concentration of 0.25 μg/mL to distinguish live and dead cells.
Sort for CD45+ leukocytes and EpCAM+ epithelial cells using a BD ARIA III flow cytometer or equivalent.
Lysate the sorted cells to release the virus.
Centrifuge sorted cells at approximately 230×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellets in serum-free DMEM medium to achieve a concentration of 10^6 cells/mL.
Freeze and thaw cells twice by alternating immersing samples in liquid nitrogen and a water bath set at 37°C.
Centrifuge lysates at approximately 10,000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C to remove debris.
Use the supernatant, undiluted or serially diluted tenfold, as inoculum for performing the plaque assay according to steps #33–41.
Homogenize frozen lungs collected in step 11 with 1 mL of serum-free DMEM medium using a mechanical homogenizer for approximately 10 seconds at maximum speed (30,000 rpm).
Centrifuge the homogenized lung samples at approximately 10,000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Use the supernatant undiluted or 10-fold serially diluted as inoculum for plaque assay according to steps #33–41.
Fix the cells by resuspending the pellet in 100 μL of 4% PFA, vortex the tubes, and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Wash the cells with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Permeabilize the cells by resuspending the pellet in 100 μL of 0.5% saponin.
Minimize intracellular unspecific antibody binding by incubation with an anti-mouse CD16/32 antibody (Fc blocking diluted 1:100) for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Stain the cells intracellularly by adding FITC-conjugated influenza A anti-NP antibody (10 μg/mL) directly to the cell suspension and incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash the cells once with permeabilization buffer.
Wash the cells again with FACS buffer.
Analyze on a BD ARIA III flow cytometer or equivalent.
Use unstained samples and single-stained samples to set appropriate PMT voltages for positive and negative populations.
Perform 10 μm-thick cryosections of OCT-embedded tissues collected in step #12 using a cryotome.
Place up to 3 sections on the same slide in the sagittal plane of the left lung lobe at the level of the respiratory tree.
Store cryosections until further use in a slide box at −20°C with silica gel to absorb moisture.
Let slides air-dry at room temperature (RT).
Define areas around sections with a hydrophobic pen.
Fix sections with 4% PFA for 10 min at RT.
Wash the slides 3 times with PBS.
Block unspecific antibody binding with 5% goat serum for 30 min at RT.
Stain sections with FITC-conjugated IAV anti-NP antibody (5 μg/mL) for 1 h at RT in the dark.
Stain for cell-specific markers in parallel to NP staining.
Add the anti-NP antibody together with secondary antibodies if unconjugated antibodies are used.
Wash slides 3× with PBS.
Stain nuclei with 2.5 μg/mL of DAPI diluted in PBS for 3 min at RT in the dark.
Rinse slides briefly in PBS.
Mount sections with Prolong Diamond mounting medium and coverslip.
Visualize with a Leica TCS-SP5II Confocal Microscope.
